Bullies animal clinic [6266]

By: Tarryn Crossman | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Unique Selling Point:
Two weeks ago, 10 dogs were dropped off at Bullies animal clinic in Pretoria to be sterilised by Dr Moos. Only 2 survived. According to the autopsy report from Onderstepoort all the dogs where given Anaesthetic that had gone off, 1 dog was overdosed on Anaesthetic, and another one had septicemia. 2 of the dogs were buried by the owner before and investigation could take place.

But this is just the latest in a series of cases against this vet, going back almost 10 years.
She has been found guilty by the SAVC and given a suspended sentence until Jan 2022. Between May 2017 - Jan 2017 she was forbidden to practice while the investigation was on going. But according to assistant Mandy, she practiced regardless. Mandy reported this to the SAVC, but nothing was done.


Summary:
Previous staff
Mandy worked with Moos from 2015 – 2019
As part her NGO, be wise sterilise, Mandy volunteered at Moos every Sunday to help with cheap sterilisation.
Dogs and cats started dying during the sterilisation sessions, her NGO had autopsies done. Onderstepoort found an overdose of Anaesthetic in at least 3 of the 10 cases they sent in.
Mandy saw Moos drunk and wetting herself at the practice, she reported everything to SAVC, but has heard nothing back.

Megan 2018 – 2020
Megan was a teenager when she started volunteering at Bullies
She has no qualifications at all but was soon instructed by Moos to administer intravenous drugs. She started topping up anaesthetic during surgery, which according to experts is not best practice but it happens. Then she became the one who put the dogs under prior to surgery, which is completely illegal and life-threatening.
During a few sterilisation Moos was so drunk she instructed Megan to close the animals up. Moos also made Megan perform a C-section on a cat the sterilisation afterwards.

Megan has videos of herself in theatre and photos showing how Moos would keep the aesthetic on the counter tops. The aesthetic used on dogs and cats is egg based and can only be used once off, then it must be discarded. According to everyone that has worked there, she uses it over a week and never puts it in the fridge, which would explain the recent contaminations

Betha June to December 2021
Unqualified assistant
Administered anaesthetic
Animals had to be resuscitated on the table a lot
Left because the working environment was too volatile

Confirmed by all staff:
She doesn’t weigh the animals prior to administering Anaesthetic
Moos never wears gloves or masks in theatre
She smokes in theatre between surgeries


Further information:
We have short video clips and photos from the practice May have to
Doorstop SAVC if they finally refuse an interview
Doorstop Dr Moos at her clinic

For some, dogs are more than just pets, they’re part of the family. So, when their new vet told Liz and Sebastian Cronje their puppy, Moose, needed double knee surgery, they didn’t think twice.

She said to me, This dog is in extreme pain. She made it sound like it was a matter of life and death, basically

Tragically, their blind faith in this vet would cost Moose’s life?

Moos crying video 2”

and at that stage she was called the Silverton Butcher
It was most horrific

she's killing animals for no reason.
It's enough now. It needs to stop. - cut to her face her

Moos: I am Linana Moos and I would categorize myself as a good private primary veterinarian,
MASA: you would?
Moos: Yes, I would




Dr Lanina Moos is a Pretoria based vet who’s been in practice for over 20 years. During much of that time allegations of gross misconduct have followed her from practice to practice. She’s based in Pretoria and has operated from her current premises since 2019. She calls it Bullies Animal Clinic. In an effort to get to the bottom of the claims, we tracked down 3 of her former assistants.

00:07:43:17 - 00:08:15:17
At the beginning
I was just
job shadowing
And eventually when I moved onto a full time role, I was helping her administer medication, handle the client side of things, and pretty much anything she wanted.

Meagan Olwage worked for Moos for 3 years from 2018.

While you were there, you documented some images and videos of what you saw.
if you could just describe what we're seeing here. So this is a dog that was brought in with a prolapsed
Dr. Morris was not impressed that the owner could let something like that happen the dog was put into a bathroom and left there
until Dr moos felt calmed down a bit
AND THAT she was ready to actually operate on the dog

Mandy Suurman runs a rescue organisation which did cheap sterilisations with Moos for four years from 2015.

MANDY
I have never seen her wear a mask or gloves.
Wait, you've never seen her wear gloves? No. And you've seen her operating on animals
yes
Michelle
underneath the nails there was blood, dried blood

Michelle Benade runs her own rabbit rescue service, and volunteered at Moos’ practice in 2015.

MICHELLE:
I was actually just going to help out there with animals. And when I saw okay, I was doing a lot more like a vet nurse, like a vet assistant.

Astonishingly, assistants with no qualifications would have to administer scheduled, intravenous medication.

Meagan
the process from cage to theatre was basically that we would inject anaesthetic, the animal would then be shaved and then it would be carried into the theatre

To ensure the right amount of anaesthetic is administered an animal should be weighed - something the assistants say they never saw Moos do.

MASA: So how would she know how much anaesthetic to give if you're not weighing the animal?
MANDY: I'm assuming she would guess.

Moos denies these accusations, but the goings on at Bullies were raising red flags: not least what was happening to healthy animals being sent there for sterilisation. But concrete evidence has been hard to get - until recently.

Link On the 17TH of October 10 dogs were taken to Bullies animal clinic for sterilization but only 3 survived

Maggie Steenkamp is from the orgainsation, Pretoria Animal Buddies. She’s been on Moos’s trail for years.

Maggie:
we always knew something was going to happen.
We just didn't know when. And we were very, very lucky this time to be on that immediately.

Steenkamp managed to get four of the seven dead dogs to Onderstepoort Veterinarian Academic Hospital for autopsy.

Maggie: A general dog, a young, active dog shouldn't be dying under anaesthesia and definitely not post-surgery.

We took the information we’d gathered to Dr Bronwyn van Dyk, a veterinary expert.

00:07:13:02 - 00:07:31:02
We've had people who have just matriculated being trained how to administer anaesthetic

BRONWYN
In order to administer medications, you have to be a veterinarian or a vet, nurse You can't be a layperson.
if you give too much aesthetic agent, then you can cause respiratory and cardiac depression,

The former assistants say Moos used an anaesthetic called Propofol. Once opened it should be used and the bottle discarded. But they say she’d use it on several animals for days on end. Moos denies this.

Edited
BRONWYN: it is an egg based anaesthetic agent
And as such, it can go off
when it does go off, what are the dangers of that?
So we will see septic shock and acute death, sudden death in patients.

Little Moose didn’t recover after Dr Moos’ surgery, so The Cronjes asked a veterinary professor for a second opinion.

SEBASTIAAN
he said, you can see all the toxins in his little body. So he was trying to flush out all the toxins first before he can do anything else.
MASA
Sebastian was the professor saying that Louise was given too much anaesthetic.
SEBASTIAAN: You said that's the reason you don't do patella centurions once he said because is too much for a little body like that to do too

Similarly, when the autopsy report on the four dogs that died in October finally arrived it pointed to anaesthetic complications.

BRONWYN
there was no other cause for death that was pre-existing. It's around the surgery. These dogs suffered acute heart failure and there's a variety of causes for that
Can we rule out anaesthetic?
No, no, no.it is in fact the most likely cause.
But as to what anaesthetic complication ultimately resulted in death, there's no concrete proof.
MASA: So it could have been bacterial or it could have been an overdose.
BRONWYN: Yes. Yeah.

The evidence now hard to ignore and with serious questions to answer, it was time to confront Dr Moos.

Masa: ten dogs arrive here for sterilization. Seven of the dogs die. how do you explain that?
MOOS:
The reason for these dogs dying, I cannot explain.

01:01:39:14 - 01:01:57:13
Speaker 3
What would you have to say to the cronies now,
Do you think you had a hand in what fatally ended up happening?
Propofol is a very short acting anaesthetic. So I can understand how the dog would do three days afterwards still be you know that badly influenced by the propofol
Masa: The professor did say that it was still displayed.
Moos: Okay well then if that’s what he said then okay, because obviously he's got more knowledge than me.

MASA: Dr. Morris, did you ever instruct
Michelle or Megan or Mandy to administer anaesthetic? No.
MOOS: They topped up there a is difference
MASA: Is that acceptable?
MOOS: Probably not.
MASA: That's not acceptable. And you know that because you abide by the South African Veterinary Council's rules and only you are registered vet or a registered nurse can top up. MOOS: Yes.

Not only were they administering anaesthetics - this 2018 video shows the assistant carrying out a caesarian section on a cat.

Did you ever instruct any of them, mainly Megan to operate on an animal?
It was a cat that was supposed to be euthanised.
Why did you allow Megan, who was unqualified to operate on an animal?
I don't have an answer for you. I honestly don't know.

Meagan
she was inebriated at the time
she basically stood next to me, instructed me how to on how to do it.

Doctor Moos do you have a drinking problem?
I had a drinking problem. I stopped drinking completely.
When was that?
2018. And then I had a problem again.
And when about did you have that problem?
While this was all corona
20, 20, 2021. Yes.
I can tell you went through a very rough patch
And it's unfortunate, but it doesn't excuse these very heavy allegations. It doesn't excuse things like people accusing you of being physically violent with the animals. Have you been physically violent with the animals
I honestly can't tell you yes or no. I dunno.

In 2019, as she was wrestling with sobriety, another video shows Dr Moos dragging a dog by its leash.

Do you think you've got some preventable deaths?
Yeah, I honestly don't know.

Ultimately, the Veterinary Council is the governing body responsible for policing Dr Moos’s conduct. It confirmed that for drinking on the job and other complaints Bernade laid, Moos was given a suspended sentence from 2017 to 2022… on condition she stayed sober. But when the other two assistants told the Council Moos was still drinking in 2019 and 20, nothing happened.

They just keep saying, we are sending the inquiry to the inquiry board. We'll get back to you.

The Cronjes’ complaint to the Council from January this year hasn’t been addressed either.

In that time, so many people still going to take the animals to this woman so she can just keep slaughtering, keep doing this to other animals

The Veterinary Council declined an on-camera interview, citing legal complications but confirmed in writing that it will have a trial in February 2023 to address the allegations made by Olwage, Suurman and the Cronjes. Until then, Moos continues to practise.

I dunno

metadata.Unique Selling Point: Two weeks ago, 10 dogs were dropped off at Bullies animal clinic in Pretoria to be sterilised by Dr Moos. Only 2 survived. According to the autopsy report from Onderstepoort all the dogs where given Anaesthetic that had gone off, 1 dog was overdosed on Anaesthetic, and another one had septicemia. 2 of the dogs were buried by the owner before and investigation could take place. But this is just the latest in a series of cases against this vet, going back almost 10 years. She has been found guilty by the SAVC and given a suspended sentence until Jan 2022. Between May 2017 - Jan 2017 she was forbidden to practice while the investigation was on going. But according to assistant Mandy, she practiced regardless. Mandy reported this to the SAVC, but nothing was done.
metadata.Summary: Previous staff Mandy worked with Moos from 2015 – 2019 As part her NGO, be wise sterilise, Mandy volunteered at Moos every Sunday to help with cheap sterilisation. Dogs and cats started dying during the sterilisation sessions, her NGO had autopsies done. Onderstepoort found an overdose of Anaesthetic in at least 3 of the 10 cases they sent in. Mandy saw Moos drunk and wetting herself at the practice, she reported everything to SAVC, but has heard nothing back. Megan 2018 – 2020 Megan was a teenager when she started volunteering at Bullies She has no qualifications at all but was soon instructed by Moos to administer intravenous drugs. She started topping up anaesthetic during surgery, which according to experts is not best practice but it happens. Then she became the one who put the dogs under prior to surgery, which is completely illegal and life-threatening. During a few sterilisation Moos was so drunk she instructed Megan to close the animals up. Moos also made Megan perform a C-section on a cat the sterilisation afterwards. Megan has videos of herself in theatre and photos showing how Moos would keep the aesthetic on the counter tops. The aesthetic used on dogs and cats is egg based and can only be used once off, then it must be discarded.
